item.title: Veterans Day 2026 brings free meals at popular restaurants — and some deals don't end Nov. 11
item.description: About 30 restaurants are offering Veterans Day deals on Nov. 11, from Outback Steakhouse's free Bloomin' Onion to Buffalo Wild Wings' boneless wings.
item.content:encoded:
Veterans and active-duty military members can find free food and other promotions at restaurants across the country on Veterans Day, Nov. 11. Some offers also give customers a reason to return for another deal later.

About 30 restaurant brands are included in Dinova's 2026 Veterans Day Dining Guide, according to Alison Quinn, the company's Florida-based president. 

The guide is in its fifth year and includes national and regional chains like Bonefish Grill, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Hooters, Outback Steakhouse and Red Lobster.

102-YEAR-OLD NAVY VETERAN STILL CRAVES HOT WINGS AFTER 102 COMBAT MISSIONS IN KOREA: 'I MIGHT MAKE IT TO 115'

"What we're starting to see now is it's going beyond Veterans Day, to try to give back to the vets in a way that is more meaningful," Quinn told Fox News Digital. "Just not about one day but come back, and we'll give you something again."

Quinn pointed to California-based Hofman Hospitality Group, which is offering select meals to veterans and a $10 bonus card for a future visit. Lucille's Smokehouse Bar-B-Que is among the group's brands.

Outback Steakhouse is offering a complimentary Bloomin' Onion and soft drink, along with a meal offer for a return visit, she said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Other deals listed in the guide include 10 free boneless wings and fries at Buffalo Wild Wings, a complimentary Red's Big Tavern Burger at Red Robin, free shrimp at Red Lobster and a free All-American Smash at Smashburger.

Dinova started the guide to share offers with veterans and, in some cases, active-duty military personnel, Quinn said. The company's business dining network includes about 25,000 restaurants and 600 corporate partners, she said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Downloads of the guide have increased over the years, Quinn said, and the promotions may be useful for veterans or active-duty personnel who are struggling or "living under a tight budget."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Asked which deal she would choose, Quinn singled out Eddie Merlot's complimentary cheeseburger. Her father is an 85-year-old veteran, she said, and she plans to tell him about it.

Veterans and active-duty military members should bring identification and check with their local restaurant before visiting, Quinn said. Participation and ID requirements can vary by location and offer.

item.title: Hegseth could face new impeachment push over Ukraine aid, lawmakers warn
item.description: War Secretary Pete Hegseth could face new articles of impeachment over Ukraine military aid as House Democrats prepare to take control of Congress.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: Some House Democrats are leaving the door open to additional articles of impeachment against War Secretary Pete Hegseth over his handling of military aid to Ukraine, according to lawmakers who spoke with Fox News Digital after a failed impeachment effort led by Republican Rep. Thomas Massie.

But a conservative legal expert suggested the renewed impeachment push may be less about removing Hegseth from office than discouraging conservatives from serving in future Republican administrations.

Massie, R-Ky., told Fox News Digital that while he could not substantiate allegations that Hegseth improperly withheld military assistance to Ukraine, he believes Democrats will investigate the matter and potentially introduce additional articles of impeachment when they take control of Congress in January.

"I believe [Democrats] may use some of the same articles of impeachment when they're in the majority, but I also believe there are gonna be some other articles of impeachment based on hearings and committees," Massie told Fox News Digital. "I think the Democrats will do that."

DEMOCRATS RALLY BEHIND GOP LAWMAKER'S HEGSETH IMPEACHMENT PUSH, SIGNAL MORE TO COME IN JANUARY

"I heard that as one of the complaints that wasn't in my impeachment resolution," Massie added.

Massie acknowledged that another impeachment effort could be largely symbolic if the Senate fails to convict Hegseth, but argued that the proceedings could still pressure the war secretary to resign.

While impeachment requires a simple majority in the House, conviction and removal from office require a two-thirds majority in the Senate.

Massie said he hopes a Democratic-controlled Senate would hold a trial if the House impeaches Hegseth.

"So there's still a reason to proceed," Massie said.

His remarks came after the House rejected his effort Tuesday to impeach Hegseth over military operations against Iran and suspected drug smugglers in the Atlantic and Pacific oceans without congressional authorization.

The Constitution grants Congress the power to declare war, while the president, as commander in chief, has authority to direct military operations. The extent to which a president can initiate hostilities without congressional authorization remains legally disputed.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., also called on the House Monday to impeach Hegseth and urged the Senate to hold a trial to remove him from office.

Schumer did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Zach Smith, a legal fellow at the Heritage Foundation, criticized Democrats' plans to pursue impeachment and potential prosecution of Trump administration officials, calling the efforts an "unfortunate waste of time" given the two-thirds Senate majority required to convict and remove an impeached official.

Smith argued, however, that Democrats are prioritizing impeachment proceedings to discourage conservatives from serving in future Republican administrations, not to actually remove Hegseth. 

He added that the efforts would also divert congressional attention from "the many very important issues that our country is facing today," including concerns Democrats campaigned on ahead of the midterm elections, such as driving down the cost of living. 

"Not only does this mean that the House and the Senate will have to take time away from the legislative activities they should be focusing on, but it will also make it more difficult for members of the Trump administration to do their duties as well, because they'll have to be dealing with these requests and other efforts by Congress," Smith told Fox News Digital.

Despite Smith's concerns, Rep. Adelita Grijalva, D-Ariz., echoed Massie's expectations, telling Fox News Digital that she anticipates congressional oversight committees will investigate Hegseth's handling of military assistance to Ukraine.

Grijalva said she expects congressional committees to hold hearings examining Hegseth's handling of Ukraine funding.

‘LAWYER UP’: DEMS IMMEDIATELY PUT TRUMP ON NOTICE AMID REPUBLICANS' MIDTERM BLOODBATH

"This is an issue that will come up again, because once we have more information into how bad his handling has been, we will likely have more movement and possibly more articles of impeachment," Grijalva told Fox News Digital.

The Arizona Democrat, who described herself as "a big believer in process and getting the facts out," argued that voters sent a clear message during the 2026 midterm elections.

Grijalva said Americans spoke "very clearly" when they voted, signaling that "they want to put an end to the corruption."

Fox News Digital could not independently verify the allegation that Hegseth improperly withheld Ukraine funding or engaged in any wrongdoing related to the matter.

Hegseth did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Rep.-elect Scott Wiener, D-Calif., told Fox News Digital that he had "no idea" whether additional impeachment articles would be introduced and was unaware of evidence supporting the allegations. However, he expressed support for removing Hegseth from office.

"I will fully support impeaching him," Wiener told Fox News Digital. "He's a disaster to our military and our country."

Republicans, meanwhile, accused Democrats of pursuing politically motivated impeachment proceedings against Trump administration officials.

House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast, R-Fla., told Fox News Digital following Tuesday's vote that he was "not surprised" by Democrats' interest in impeaching Hegseth.

Mast argued that Democrats were determined to impeach "anyone who was appointed by the president," regardless of whether evidence supported the allegations.

The discussions come as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January, giving the party greater power to launch investigations, hold hearings and pursue impeachment proceedings.

item.title: Country star Craig Morgan says he's 'willing to die' for America after returning to military service
item.description: Craig Morgan says he's willing to die for America's freedoms as the U.S. Army reserve officer releases his patriotic new album "My Country."
item.content:encoded:
Country singer Craig Morgan, a U.S. Army Reserve warrant officer, says he is willing to die for his country to preserve America's freedoms.

"I am willing to go wherever they send me and do whatever it takes to ensure that we maintain the freedoms," Morgan, who reenlisted in the Army in 2023 after previously serving for nearly two decades, told Fox News Digital. "And not for me, but for my family, for my friends, for my friend's kids, and for the kids that I don't even know."

He said he thinks every American service member feels the same way he does.

AARON TIPPIN SAYS PATRIOTISM IS 'VERY STRONG IN AMERICA' AHEAD OF FORT CAMPBELL 4TH OF JULY SHOW

"Listen, like the [Toby Keith] song ‘American Soldier’ says, ‘I don't want to die, but if dying is asked of me, I will.’ And I believe that more people, even those that don't serve, feel that way."

The "Redneck Yacht Club" singer, who lives in Tennessee, said, "That's what we celebrate."

LEE GREENWOOD SAYS HE'S 'VERY PROUD' TO STAND NEXT TO TRUMP DURING AMERICA'S 250TH CELEBRATION

"But absolutely, I am willing to die for my country and to die for the freedoms that I get to celebrate. I want my grandchildren and their children and their grandchildren to celebrate those same freedoms."

Morgan released a new 11-song album, "My Country," on Nov. 6, which features a cover of "American Soldier."

CARRIE UNDERWOOD, GARY SINISE LEAD STARS WHO'VE SHARED WHY THEY'RE PROUD TO BE AMERICANS

"We're celebrating our 250th," he said. "I just felt like it was most appropriate as we celebrate that as a nation that I'm able to do it in my genre, in my format, in my occupation."

WATCH: CRAIG MORGAN SAYS HE IS WILLING TO DIE FOR HIS COUNTRY

He said he feels like he’s always celebrating America, "but we took it, I feel like we took it a step further with this actual project, a physical project, celebrating our nation, hence the name ‘My Country,’ but for me, it had a dual implication."

COUNTRY STAR CHRIS JANSON SAYS RESPECTING THE FLAG IS THE NUMBER ONE LESSON HE WANTS HIS KIDS TO LEARN

At the risk of sounding biased, Morgan said he thinks country music "celebrates the love and passion for our freedom and for our nation much more than the other genres."

KID ROCK TAPS EMINEM FOR CHRISTIAN ALBUM, PLANS BEER-AND-FAITH ARENA REVIVALS

"We don't shy away or steer away from our belief in God, family, and country," he added, "and this project really kind of hits at both of those, both of my worlds, my military world and my music world."

The 62-year-old is especially proud of the original track "Long May You Wave," which he called "extremely personal" and emotional.

BLACK RIFLE COFFEE CO-FOUNDER RELEASES NEW MUSIC VIDEO HONORING FALLEN SOLDIERS AHEAD OF MEMORIAL DAY

"Having served in the military for over 20 years now, that flag represents something that I think — there was a time in our nation that it had been taken for granted. I do believe that we're back in a place where we respect that flag, we respect what it stands for. And I'm not saying that we didn't, but I think generally we lost sight of what it is that flag represented and the many, many men and women who have sacrificed in order to ensure that that representation is not tarnished."

The song is about middle-class America — "the people that really built this country and the people whose backs we stand on," he said.

DOLLY PARTON'S ‘ALL-AMERICAN HEART’: HOW COUNTRY ICON FORGED SPECIAL BOND WITH US MILITARY

The cover of "American Soldier" is in honor of Keith "and in honor of what he stood for," he explained.

"For me, that song again is extremely personal," he said. "I am an American soldier and I love my country and I love what this song says about us."

Morgan said service members don’t "stand out there and wave our flag, so to speak, but this song is a testament to, in my opinion, the moral fiber that makes up those people who serve our nation. And I'm grateful to have the honor to be able to record that song."

WATCH: CRAIG MORGRAN ON WHY HE'S RELEASING HIS PATRIOTIC ‘MY COUNTRY’ ALBUM NOW

He added that country music offers listeners a "sense of reality, a sense of truth. Also, all of this wrapped up in humility, grace, and gratitude."

"The general populace of the country music format, including the artists, come from a place of humble beginnings, come from a place of Middle America," he said. "We talk about, sing about, and represent, and live the lifestyle of the people that build America, as I alluded to earlier. And I still live that lifestyle. A lot of people don't believe it. I mean, you know, I don't always cut my own grass, but I do sometimes, but I still take off my own garbage when I'm home."

Speaking about his own family, Morgan said he hopes his grandchildren "inherit the attitude towards our nation that my grandfather had and that I feel like I have."

"One thing that I see now that I did not see four years ago is a sense of pride in our nation, a sense of pride in their jobs," he said.

He said he doesn’t preach his politics, "but here's what I tell every one of them: If we are not a safe nation, all of the other stuff that you celebrate will not matter. It's that simple."

Morgan also held a Veterans Day 5K in Nashville on Veterans Day this year to bring attention to the charities he supports and raise money for them and to celebrate veterans.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Equally important to Morgan is his faith.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Morgan said he’s faced pushback in the entertainment industry over it, "but when it comes to my faith in my God, I do not care. I can't. I focus solely on my relationship with my God through my church and allow that to dictate. Whatever happens outside of that is on them, not me."

He’s fine with people disagreeing with him, and he doesn’t want to convert everyone, "because that's God's job. I just live my life in accordance with the word as best I can, focus on my relationship with him and hope that I'm doing the things that he would have me do so that people can come to know him through me."

item.title: Ilhan Omar appears clueless on basis for federal probes: ‘You probably have more details on that’
item.description: Ilhan Omar told reporters she was never informed what federal agencies are specifically investigating, even questioning if multiple probes exist.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., told Fox News Digital on Tuesday she was never informed by federal agencies of the grounds on which she is being investigated — even claiming she isn’t sure how many probes into her there are.

"No, no," she said when asked if she had been told exactly the basis for the investigations.

There are two known ongoing federal probes into the Somali-born congresswoman — the first, confirmed by sources to Fox News Digital, is the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) looking into whether her immigration paperwork was fraudulently filled out by herself or her father; and the second is investigating her financial disclosures discrepancies and was confirmed publicly by U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro.

ILHAN OMAR'S TURBULENT WEEK EXPLAINED: THE DUELING PROBES THAT THREW THE SOMALI-BORN PROGRESSIVE INTO CHAOS

On Omar’s first day back on Capitol Hill following the investigations, she told Fox News Digital she doesn't know if DHS and the Department of Justice (DOJ) are each investigating her independently.

"I’m not sure," Omar said. "You probably have more details on that."

The congresswoman's feigned innocence on the matter came after she had a two-hour meeting with her lawyers at her Capitol Hill office on Tuesday.

The news of the federal investigations first gained steam after Fox News Digital first reported that agents with Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) were executing a federal raid on Omar’s Washington, D.C., residence on Oct. 12. Sources confirmed the search was in relation to an investigation into Omar's immigration paperwork.

The Somali-born lawmaker arrived in the U.S. in 1995 as a refugee fleeing civil war after spending four years in a refugee camp in Kenya.

ILHAN OMAR HUDDLES WITH HER DC-BASED LAWYERS DURING HER FIRST DAY BACK ON CAPITOL HILL AMID FEDERAL PROBES

Federal agents reportedly seized the congresswoman’s cellphone, passport and computer. Fox News Digital also later confirmed that a sample of the congresswoman’s DNA was also obtained during the raid.

Omar told Fox News Digital on Tuesday that "most" of the items seized during the raid have been returned to her possession.

"I’ve gotten most of them back," Omar said.

More information continues to come to light as the investigations proceed, including a federal court filing identifying Omar by the name "Ilhan Nur Said Elmi," which matches the last name of her ex-husband, whom reports have alleged is her brother.

The marriage continues to draw scrutiny after the Daily Caller recently reported that her ex-husband Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, who is alleged to be her brother, described himself as a "gay man" in an academic paper that was published earlier this year.

OBAMA ADMIN FIRST LAUNCHED THE INVESTIGATION INTO ILHAN OMAR'S ALLEGED BROTHER MARRIAGE

Omar ignored Fox News Digital’s questioning about her ex-husband and rumored brother referring to himself as "gay" in Aug. 2026, just months before HSI raided her house and federal investigations got underway.

The congresswoman is still under investigation as she returns to Capitol Hill after winning re-election to represent Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District. Her two high-profile lawyers, Amy Jeffress and Joshua Matz, were seen leaving her office in the Longworth House Office Building after a roughly two-hour meeting.

Omar’s team did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

item.title: USA hockey hero Connor Hellebuyck greeted with 'Trump's your daddy,' other vulgar chants in return to Winnipeg
item.description: Connor Hellebuyck faced hostile chants from Winnipeg Jets fans in his return, with crowds referencing Trump and the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
item.content:encoded:
USA Olympic hockey hero Connor Hellebuyck made his return to his former Canadian home on Tuesday night, and Winnipeg Jets fans let him hear it.

The star goaltender, who stopped 41 of Team Canada's 42 shots en route to winning gold, requested a trade from the Jets and landed with the New Jersey Devils last month, teaming him up with Jack Hughes, who scored the golden goal back in February.

The Devils made the controversial decision to not have Hellebuyck in net, citing a potential "reduction in our expected win probability."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Hellebuyck, though, was the backup for the night and still took the ice for warmups and got the wrath of the Jets faithful.

He was hit with chants, some explicit, from "coward" and "We don't miss you" to "Trump's your daddy" — President Donald Trump singled out Hellebuyck in his phone call with the team after winning gold and announced he would receive the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian honor.

Hellebuyck insisted that he felt it was his "duty" to play, but the front office had other decisions.

TEAM USA HERO CONNOR HELLEBUYCK SAYS THAT MOMENTS BEYOND ONLINE DEATH THREATS LED TO HIS WINNIPEG DEPARTURE

Hellebuyck was somewhat mum on his reasons for wanting a trade aside from joining a team he views as a contender, but that changed on Tuesday.

Hellebuyck said there was no single moment that led to him wanting out, and that some off-ice issues played into it, saying he had faced "more than online death threats."

Dawson Mercer, who was sent to the Jets from the Devils in the trade, put two pucks past Jake Allen to help Winnipeg win, 3-2. Nico Daws, also now a former Devil, was in net for the Jets.

item.title: Bernie Sanders says he won't back Schumer as push for new leadership gains steam
item.description: Bernie Sanders and Elissa Slotkin say they will not support Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader, calling for a new generation of leadership.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., says he will not support Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., to serve as Senate majority leader once Democrats take control over the chamber next year.

Sanders was complimentary of Schumer, but said at a news conference on Tuesday that he believes "the time is now" for change in Democratic leadership.

"I personally have known Chuck Schumer for over 30 years, and I like Chuck. [There’s] nobody who works harder than Chuck Schumer. But in my view, the time is now for change, and I will not be supporting Chuck to be re-elected as the Democratic leader," Sanders said at a news conference.

CHUCK SCHUMER AFTER SWEEPING DEMOCRATIC MIDTERM VICTORIES: 'I'LL BE RE-ELECTED AS MAJORITY LEADER'

Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., joined Sanders at the Tuesday news conference and said she also will not be supporting Schumer. Neither has backed a specific candidate to replace Schumer, however.

"I am not actively seeking this job. I am seeking change," Slotkin said. "I’ve been very consistent for a very long time that we need a new generation of leadership … It’s important to demonstrate that we’ve heard what people want from this last election."

THE HITCHHIKER’S GUIDE TO WHAT HAPPENS NEXT ON CAPITOL HILL

Sanders and Slotkin join many Senate newcomers in opposing Schumer's re-election, including the likes of Sens.-elect Adam Hamilton and Troy Jackson.

A number of the more left-wing Democrats favor Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., for the new leader.

SCHUMER DUCKS QUESTION ON CAMPAIGNING WITH SOCIALIST CANDIDATE WHO REFUSES TO BACK HIM AS LEADER

"I’ve said very clearly that we need to have a discussion in the Democratic caucus," Van Hollen said during an appearance at Crooked Con over the weekend.

"We need to understand what the Democrats are going to do with this new responsibility and these new powers," he continued. "And that nobody should get a blank check without a full understanding from the caucus as to where we’re going to go."

And Van Hollen, who has previously said his focus was more on "kicking the tires" on a run for higher office in 2028, is reportedly mulling a bid for Schumer’s job, according to Politico.

Fox News' Alex Miller contributed to this report.

item.title: Historic US ship that once ruled the Atlantic faces extraordinary fate near Florida
item.description: Once the fastest Atlantic ocean liner, the SS United States is set to become the world's largest artificial reef in a $13.5 million project off the coast of Florida.
item.content:encoded:
The SS United States, a historic ship that was once the fastest ocean liner to cross the Atlantic, is meeting its fate Wednesday. 

The ship is scheduled to be sunk off Florida's coast as part of plans to make it the world's largest artificial reef, a $13.5 million project aimed at benefiting divers, fishing enthusiasts and marine life alike, according to The Associated Press (AP).

Built in Virginia in 1950 and 1951, the ship in its time carried famous passengers including President John F. Kennedy, former King Edward VIII, Grace Kelly and Elizabeth Taylor.

HAUNTING NEW IMAGES REVEAL THE FINAL SHIP WHERE EXPLORER SIR ERNEST SHACKLETON DIED

It also once took a young Bill Clinton to Oxford University in 1968 before being decommissioned a year later.

But in the decades since, the ship fell into disrepair. The reef project is intended to prevent it from becoming scrap metal.

The SS United States sat along a dock in Philadelphia from 1996 until February 2025, the AP reported.

The ship is expected to sink in about 180 feet of water, roughly 25 miles southwest of Destin, Florida. 

Its top deck will rest about 60 feet below the surface, making it accessible to recreational divers — and it will sit near about 500 other artificial reefs.

'SPECTACULAR' SHIPWRECK FOUND WITH UNDERWATER TIME CAPSULE OF UNTOUCHED CARGO: 'AMAZING FIND'

Alicia Johnson, a Maine-based maritime archaeologist and head of digital engagement at Accupixel, told Fox News Digital she has mixed feelings about the ship's transformation into an artificial reef.

"As a scuba diver, I'm thrilled at the prospect of a new underwater site to visit and photograph, as well as the benefits it could potentially reap for the marine environment," she said.

"However, as a maritime archeologist, I'm concerned about preserving the historic fabric of the ship."

DIVERS UNCOVER HUNDREDS OF ANCIENT RELICS NEAR SHIPWRECK UNTOUCHED FOR 2,100 YEARS

To prepare for the sinking, organizers removed the ship's 65-foot smokestacks, which are expected to be displayed in a future museum, according to the AP.

Crews also removed tanks once used in the ship's cooling system so that seawater can flood the hull when valves are opened.

More than 400 portholes were removed, and large holes were cut into the decks.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER UNEXPECTED TWIST IN SHIPWRECK MYSTERY AFTER CLUES DON'T ADD UP

Johnson said it's also important to document the ship before it is submerged, since its original condition cannot be recreated once it is underwater.

"Once the ship is submerged, we cannot replicate the state it was in prior to its submersion," she said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

She recommended using laser scanning, photographs and detailed drawings to create a digital record of the vessel.

She also suggested preserving historic artifacts in museums where they can be accessed by the public.

Johnson said the sinking also presents a rare opportunity for researchers to study how a ship changes underwater over time.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

While many shipwrecks are discovered decades or even centuries after they sink, researchers will be able to study the SS United States from the moment it enters the water.

"We get to study this ship from the moment before it goes in the water to 10, 20, 30 years after it's been in the water," she said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"So as a maritime archeologist, I think it's going to be very exciting as a case study because it doesn't necessarily categorize itself as a traditional archeological site," added Johnson.

Though the ship's days above water are coming to an end, Johnson said its historical significance will live on.

"These aren't sites just for scuba divers. They're the history of our ancestors, the history of our societies," she said. 

The Associated Press contributed reporting.

item.title: Multiple Kennedy family members seek to join legal battle against Trump's triumphal arch
item.description: Kennedy family members are seeking to join legal actions challenging plans to build President Donald Trump's triumphal arch, which he wants built in Washington, D.C.
item.content:encoded:
Nine members of the Kennedy family sought on Tuesday to join litigation opposing President Donald Trump's bid to build a triumphal arch in the nation's capital.

"President Donald J. Trump is attempting to unlawfully erect a massive arch that will permanently cast shadows over and damage historically significant sightlines to the existing gravesites and memorials established in the Kennedy family’s honor at Arlington National Cemetery, as well as to the memorials of hundreds of thousands of fallen American heroes," their complaint asserted.

FEDERAL JUDGE TEMPORARILY BLOCKS CONSTRUCTION OF TRUMP'S ARLINGTON TRIUMPHAL ARCH HOURS AFTER APPROVAL

"The plaintiffs include Rory Kennedy, Maxwell Kennedy, Christopher G. Kennedy, Kerry Kennedy, Courtney Kennedy, the Hon. Kathleen Kennedy Townsend, and the Hon. Joseph P. Kennedy II, children of Sen. Robert F. Kennedy and Ethel Kennedy; the Hon. Joseph P. Kennedy III, a grandchild of Robert and Ethel Kennedy; and Edward M. Kennedy, Jr., son of Sen. Edward M. Kennedy," according to a Democracy Defenders Fund press release.

Rory and Maxwell Kennedy discussed the issue in a statement on the family's behalf.

"This action is about protecting sacred spaces that belong to the American people. Our parents, Robert and Ethel Kennedy, and our uncles, President John F. Kennedy and Senator Edward M. Kennedy, are laid to rest at Arlington National Cemetery. Our uncle Joseph P. Kennedy Jr., who lost his life serving our country in World War II, is also memorialized there. They are among the more than 400,000 veterans and family members buried or honored on this hallowed ground. We believe Donald Trump has violated the laws and procedures established by Congress to protect this most sacred national memorial. In bringing this lawsuit, we stand for those who can not stand for themselves.

LAWYER SAYS 250-FOOT TRUMP ARCH DISRUPTS HISTORIC SIGHTLINES CHERISHED BY VETERANS SEEKING BURIAL AT ARLINGTON

"Americans from every corner of the country visit Arlington to honor those who served and sacrificed for our nation. A towering arch casting shadows across the graves of our father, mother, and uncles, as well as the graves of so many who have served our country, would also cast a shadow over our democratic principles, undermining the safeguards established by our elected representatives to protect this hallowed ground for generations to come. Our lawsuit asks the administration to respect the sanctity of Arlington National Cemetery, the laws established to protect it, and the rights of all Americans who come here to honor those who have served our country," the family's statement said.

Last week, a federal judge temporarily blocked the Trump administration from breaking ground on the proposed triumphal arch, shortly after a federal planning commission approved the project. U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan issued a 14-day temporary restraining order halting construction.

White House spokesman Davis Ingle issued this statement on Wednesday to Fox News Digital: "An activist district court has temporarily blocked the construction of the long-awaited Arch. It is unfortunate to see that some members of the Kennedy family have joined the litigation against the Arch as the project is intended to honor our heroes who rest in Arlington Cemetery. The judiciary should not be abused to politicize a structure designed to unite our nation. We will continue making the case for this beautiful and fitting monument and are confident we will be fully vindicated as this litigation proceeds. We look forward to seeing the completion of this magnificent Arch—a tribute to 250 years of American greatness."

Trump has said the arch would be utilized for military purposes.

TRUMP SAYS NEW ARCH WILL ALSO DEPLOY DRONES, POSITION SNIPERS AND STORE AMMO

"At the strong request of the United States Military, and for National Security purposes, I have agreed to convert the magnificent Triumphal Arch, planned since the Civil War Era many years ago, at the Receptive Circle adjoining the Arlington Memorial Bridge, into a top grade Military Complex/Triumphal Arch, to house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large numbers of drones, plus Snipers, on both the roof and plaza areas, and additionally have and hold large quantities of sniper ammunition in storage," he said in a Sept. 20 Truth Social post.

Fox News Digital's Michael Sinkewicz contributed to this report.

item.title: ‘He blamed the Jews’: GOP congressman levels explosive accusation against JD Vance over election postmortem
item.description: Rep. Randy Fine compared JD Vance's post-midterm election analysis to 1932 Germany, saying the vice president tacitly blamed Jewish people for GOP losses.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Randy Fine, R-Fla., said Vice President JD Vance's election analysis posted online last week amounted to an attack on the Jewish people, leading him to swear off support for any presidential aspirations Vance might have for 2028.

"I definitively will not be supporting the vice president in that nominating contest. I thought his message that he put out the day after the election was abhorrent and, frankly, smacked of the kind of thing you’d read in 1932 Germany," Fine, who is himself Jewish, said in an interview with Fox Now.

"He’s out in my book," he added. "He blamed the Jews for losing the election."

VANCE COURTING DISGRUNTLED TRUMP VOTERS TO FORM ‘NEW RIGHT’ ALLIANCE AFTER REPUBLICAN BLOODBATH, SOURCES SAY

Fine’s blistering attack on Vance comes as the GOP is working to understand the midterm election results, in which Republicans lost control of the U.S. House of Representatives and the Senate. It also underscores tensions in the GOP as the party wrestles with how to balance America-First principles with its alliance with Israel.

In his breakdown, Vance cited polling that identified four key items disillusioned voters wanted to see from Republicans: ending the war in Iran, focusing on the cost of living, putting America first and changing the U.S.-Israel relationship.

"Our voters showed up. And the above four reasons are why many of them voted for Democrats," Vance wrote.

Amid that mix, Vance especially singled out the first item, noting that Trump had himself identified the Iran conflict as a decisive factor in the midterms in interviews after the election.

"The reason we lost is the war," Vance said. "The president himself said so last night."

But Fine had a different diagnosis.

When asked about his comments by Fox News Digital, Fine doubled down on his characterization, arguing that the vice president had tacitly laid blame on "the Jews" in three of the four reasons he had identified.

RUBIO'S DEFENSE OF TRUMP'S IRAN WAR DRAWS SHARP CONTRAST WITH VANCE'S MIDTERM BLAME

"What does America First mean when you've said, ‘end the war’ and ‘change our relationship with Israel?’ Isn't that saying the same thing? When you hear… talk about America First, are they saying, ‘let's stop giving aid to Egypt?’ No, it's always about Israel. So it's three times out of four things," Fine said.

Although Vance’s election breakdown didn’t mention Jews specifically, Fine believes the connection between Israel as a state and the Jewish people is inseparable.

"You can't be Jewish if you don't believe in Israel. It's core to our identity and who we are," Fine said.

Fine also believes there is a distinction between Trump’s view of the war in Iran and the breakdown expressed by Vance. In particular, Fine highlighted comments from Trump in which the president said he would likely do the war over again if given the opportunity.

"The president said it himself. He said, I would do it again knowing what I know now because they can't have a nuclear weapon," Fine said.

"I'm not sure JD Vance is bothered by the idea of Iran having a nuclear weapon," he added.

Vance’s office declined to respond to the characterization.

ROBERT L MAGINNIS: IRAN WAR COST REPUBLICANS CONGRESS. WHAT WILL IT COST AMERICA?

Fine has been one of Israel’s loudest supporters in the House of Representatives. He has introduced several pro-Israel pieces of legislation, such as the Enhanced Iran Sanctions Act of 2025, argued that the U.S. should recognize the Muslim Brotherhood, a political-religious organization, as a terrorist organization, and urged the U.S. to officially designate the Palestinian-controlled West Bank with the Jewish historical names of "Judea and Samaria."

He encouraged Republicans to steer clear of seeing Israel as the reason why the GOP underperformed in the midterm elections.

"If you don't identify the true reasons for the failure, you will fail again, which is why JD Vance can't be our nominee because he doesn't understand the reason that we lost the election," Fine said.

item.title: Newly elected NJ Democrat repeatedly dodges question on whether Iran is our adversary
item.description: New Jersey Democratic Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy repeatedly dodged CNN's Pamela Brown when asked whether he views Iran or Israel as a U.S. adversary.
item.content:encoded:
New Jersey Democratic Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy struggled to answer whether he viewed Iran as an adversary and Israel as an ally to the U.S. on Tuesday.

During an interview on CNN's "The Situation Room," co-host Pamela Brown repeatedly asked Hamawy about his views on both of the countries regarding his demand that the U.S. pull all military funding from Israel in the wake of the war with Iran.

"Well, now, what I see is that we were pushed into this war by Israel," Hamawy said. "It's not helping Americans. Americans didn't ask for it. It's illegal and immoral. And at this point, I think the U.S. and the Iranians want this war to end."

RAHM EMANUEL ACCUSES ANTI-ISRAEL DEMS OF HAVING NO MIDDLE EAST PLAN BESIDES CUTTING FUNDING TO JEWISH STATE

"Do you see Iran as the adversary?" Brown asked.

"I see that we pushed them into a fight. And so, I think we both have to step back and say, is this helping either one of us?" Hamawy answered.

Brown repeatedly pressed Hamawy on whether he viewed Iran as an adversary, and the conressman-elect continued to avoid answering despite Brown reminding him that Iranians have chanted, "Death to America."

"We've been saying ‘Death to Iran’ for decades as well," Hamawy responded. "And so, what we need to do is use diplomacy."

"They've killed a lot of Americans," Brown said.

"And we've killed a lot of them as well," Hamawy said.

PRO-ISRAEL LEADER WARNS DEMOCRATS FAILING TO CONDEMN ‘VICIOUS JEW HATERS’ IN CONGRESS

Hamawy pushed for diplomacy over war, though Brown pointed out that he still refused to clarify his views on Iran or Israel.

"I'm saying that that doesn't help us. We're in the middle of a war right now that is making American lives worse. We're putting our troops at risk. We're creating, you know, an economic crisis that we don't need. And so, the blame game doesn't help. So, how do we get out of this?" Hamawy said.

He later referred to the Iranian government as a "dictatorship" and "authoritarian," though he suggested that America's actions have made the country more radical.

Fox News Digital reached out to Hamawy's team for comment but did not immediately hear back.

Hamawy's comments resembled Michigan Democratic Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, who refused to say whether Israel or Iran was the greater threat to America despite repeated questioning.

AOC-BACKED DEMOCRAT WITH PAST TIES TO AL QAEDA-LINKED GROUP WINS NJ HOUSE PRIMARY

"I think both of them have proven dangerous in their own way," El-Sayed said in October. "One at risk of attacking us, one getting us into wars. We have no business fighting."

Hamawy won a House seat despite scrutiny for his previous volunteer work with the Benevolence International Foundation (BIF) — a Chicago-based charity that federal authorities later identified as providing financial and logistical support to al-Qaeda. 

He was also scrutinized over his past relationship with Sheikh Omar Abdel-Rahman, commonly known as the "Blind Sheikh," whom he accompanied on a trip in 1991.

Roz Rothstein, co-founder and CEO of StandWithUs, an international nonpartisan education organization that supports Israel, condemned Hamawy's comments, accusing him of refusing to acknowledge a "moral reality."

"Representative-elect Hamawy refused to acknowledge a basic factual and moral reality. Iran's oppressive regime has made itself the enemy of both the United States and its own people. American officials who don't understand that should have no role in our country's foreign policy decisions," Rothstein told Fox News Digital.

item.title: Moderate Dem governor-elect in hot seat after signaling one of her 'top priorities' in presser: 'Resist'
item.description: Amy Klobuchar's push for Minnesota gun safety legislation drew fierce conservative backlash over a bill that would ban AR-15 sales and limit magazines.
item.content:encoded:
Minnesota Governor-elect Amy Klobuchar, who has positioned herself as a moderate during her years in Congress, is facing blowback over comments made shortly after the election suggesting she will push for gun control when she takes office.

"The gun safety bill is going to get passed, and I am so excited to be working with the leaders on this, and it certainly should be one of our top priorities," Klobuchar said during a press conference. "I think that bill makes a lot of sense. I’m sure that we’ll make some changes … but the basics of that bill I hope will remain in place."

The bill Klobuchar referenced is SF 4067, an omnibus gun-control package that passed the Minnesota Senate 34-33 earlier this year but has not received a House vote. The measure would prohibit federally licensed firearms dealers from selling certain semiautomatic military-style assault weapons, including AR-15s, as well as large-capacity magazines capable of holding more than 17 rounds.

The legislation would allow current owners to keep the covered firearms and magazines, but require them to obtain an ownership certification from the state Bureau of Criminal Apprehension and renew that certification every three years. Knowingly possessing an uncertified weapon or magazine would be a gross misdemeanor, with a subsequent violation punishable as a felony.

INSIDE TRUMP'S UNPRECEDENTED BATTLE PLAN TO EXPAND SECOND AMENDMENT RIGHTS THROUGH JUSTICE DEPARTMENT

Klobuchar quickly faced criticism from conservatives and pro-Second Amendment groups on social media, accusing her of pushing a liberal gun control agenda on law-abiding Minnesotans, particularly in rural areas.

"Democrats don't care about affordability. They only care about taking away our Second Amendment rights," conservative communicator Steve Guest posted on X. "Amy Klobuchar can't contain her excitement as she goes after law-abiding gun owners."

"In one of her first acts as governor-elect, Sen. @amyklobuchar affirmed that she will go after Minnesotans' firearms under the guise of ‘safety,’" the National Rifle Association (NRA) posted on X.

"When Amy Klobuchar told you over and over she was going to do a top-to-bottom audit, she meant of your guns, not your tax dollars," Minnesota attorney and former immigration judge Nathan Hansen posted on X.

DEMOCRATS' LATEST GUN-CONTROL PUSH RUNS INTO INCONVENIENT FACT ABOUT HOW SCHOOL KILLER WAS STOPPED

"Why are you babbling about gun control?" Minnesota Miners, a pro-mining grassroots nonprofit in Minnesota, posted on X. "Instead you should be coming out with your plan to stop government fraud and lowering taxes. But you can't do that you have to come out attacking & trying to violate lawful gun owners constitutional rights."

"We have a duty to our nation to not comply," Minnesota Republican state Rep. Ben Davis posted on X. "Resist."

"AMY KLOBUCHAR ISN'T EVEN SWORN IN AND SHE'S ALREADY COMING FOR MINNESOTA'S RIFLES," conservative influencer Gunther Eagleman posted on X.

Fox News Digital reached out to Klobuchar’s team for comment on what aspects of the bill she does and does not support but did not receive a response.

"I am committed as ever to moving our state forward, not moving our state to the left or to the right, but moving our state forward," Klobuchar said during the press conference.

Klobuchar, who has served as a Minnesota senator since 2007, defeated Minnesota Republican House Speaker Lisa Demuth 13 points in the gubernatorial election earlier this month and will take office in January, replacing Gov. Tim Walz, who dropped his re-election bid in January amid fallout from a massive fraud scandal.

item.title: Inside Holocaust memorial in heart of Arab world as founder reveals what changed everything
item.description: Inside Dubai's Crossroads of Civilizations Museum, founder Ahmed Obaid Al Mansoori reveals how a temporary Holocaust tribute became a permanent gallery.
item.content:encoded:
DUBAI, United Arab Emirates — In a historic house near Dubai Creek, a small gallery commemorating the six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust stands alongside collections exploring Islamic civilization, Emirati heritage and the history of Palestine and the Holy Land.

The Holocaust exhibition at the privately owned Crossroads of Civilizations Museum is among the first permanent displays of its kind in the Arab world. Opened in May 2021, less than a year after the UAE normalized relations with Israel through the Abraham Accords, it has become a symbol of the Emirates' approach to religious coexistence.

During a recent visit to the museum, Fox News Digital saw displays documenting Nazi persecution, including a life-size image of the boy from the famous Warsaw Ghetto photograph, his hands raised in surrender.

The gallery also tells the stories of Muslims who rescued Jews during the Holocaust, including Egyptian physician Mohammed Helmy, who sheltered Jews from Nazi persecution in Berlin.

US-BACKED ISRAEL-MOROCCO DEAL DEEPENS ABRAHAM ACCORDS AMID GROWING REGIONAL THREATS

But the story behind the exhibition is as personal as the objects it preserves.

In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, museum founder Ahmed Obaid Al Mansoori, a former member of the UAE's Federal National Council, explained that his passion for collecting historical artifacts began in childhood, when he inherited family manuscripts and objects from his grandparents.

DOMINICAN REPUBLIC JOINS GLOBAL FIGHT AGAINST ANTISEMITISM WITH LANDMARK MOVE

He began collecting systematically in 1989, eventually establishing a private museum in his home in 2006. Dubai authorities later provided a historic building to accommodate his growing collection, which opened to the public in 2014.

The Holocaust gallery came much later.

9/11 MUSEUM UNVEILS EXHIBITION FOR GENERATION TOO YOUNG TO REMEMBER THE ATTACKS: 'CALLED EVERYBODY TO LEAD'

Al Mansoori said two experiences inspired him. The first was a visit to the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum in Washington during the 1990s, where he was deeply moved by the message that the Holocaust was a tragedy with lessons for all humanity.

The second was a conversation with an American Jewish acquaintance who expressed fear about rising antisemitism in the United States. Initially, he dismissed her concerns. But after encountering antisemitic imagery circulating during a period of unrest in the U.S., he reconsidered. "I realized I was wrong," he said.

He turned to Jewish friends and colleagues to organize a Holocaust remembrance event in Dubai in 2021.

CHRISTIAN LEADERS HOLD EMERGENCY SUMMIT IN JERUSALEM TO CONFRONT GLOBAL RISE IN ANTISEMITISM

"The beauty about this Holocaust gallery was built by Arabs, by Jews, and by Christians," he told Fox News Digital, describing the international team that helped create the exhibition.

What began as a commemorative initiative became something much larger.

At the opening, Al Mansoori said, he was struck by the positive response from visitors, including residents of the UAE and people from elsewhere in the region. He also encountered criticism, but concluded that the gallery should become a permanent part of the museum.

"I thought it was very beautiful, very important. And it must stay," he recalled.

The exhibition formally opened on May 26, 2021, attended by the Israeli and German ambassadors to the UAE, according to The National's coverage at the time.

TRUMP CALLS ON ARAB NATIONS TO SIGN ABRAHAM ACCORDS

Yet Al Mansoori's vision extends beyond Holocaust remembrance.

In another section of the museum, historical maps of Palestine appear alongside Jewish manuscripts, photographs and documents illustrating the region's overlapping histories.

"You have the maps from the Israeli perspective. You have the map from the Palestinian perspective," he said, explaining why he deliberately brings different historical narratives into the same space.

He recalled a visit by rabbis in August 2020, when Muslim, Jewish and Christian guests prayed alongside one another at the museum, each according to their own traditions.

For Al Mansoori, the purpose is not to erase religious or political differences, but to make it possible for people to respect one another despite them.

"It's how to learn to be comfortable being yourself next to others. And others must be also comfortable to be next to you," he said.

As war and political tensions continue to divide the Middle East, Al Mansoori believes the museum offers a different way to confront the region's painful history: not by avoiding it, but by allowing visitors to encounter histories and experiences beyond their own.

item.title: Duke coach Jon Scheyer says Blue Devils' upset loss to Michigan State felt like an 'out-of-body experience'
item.description: Jon Scheyer called Duke's 79-73 loss to Michigan State "an out-of-body experience," vowing to fix the Blue Devils' lack of connection on the court.
item.content:encoded:
While many in the college basketball world were surprised to see Duke lose in the fashion it did to Michigan State on Tuesday night, no one was more shocked by the result than Blue Devils head coach Jon Scheyer.

Duke fell to the Spartans, 79-73, but Michigan State controlled the game from the jump. The Spartans scored the opening bucket of the contest 33 seconds after tip, and didn't allow Duke to take the lead once throughout the entire game.

While No. 2 Duke losing on a neutral floor to No. 5 Michigan State by six points won't hurt the Blue Devils' résumé, that doesn't mean Scheyer had the urge to find any positives after his team's loss.

UCONN, KANSAS AND TEXAS OFFER THE BEST COLLEGE BASKETBALL NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP ODDS VALUE

The head coach was sure to give Tom Izzo's Spartans their flowers and respect during his postgame news conference, but made it clear that he was a bit shocked by what he saw from his own team on Tuesday.

"Congrats to Michigan State," Scheyer said during his opening remarks inside the press area. "They 100 percent deserved to win. I thought they outcompeted us. They played more together."

"For me, it was a little bit of an out-of-body experience," Scheyer continued. "Our team, I thought our team, we weren't connected. Just the bottom line, we weren't connected, and we're going to fix it. I promise you that much, and our fans deserve better. That was not a good performance tonight."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The good news for the Blue Devils is that their loss to the Spartans was just their third game of the season, and they have another three-plus months to find the cohesiveness Scheyer was hoping to see against Michigan State.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

item.title: Instagram's AI may catch teens lying about their age
item.description: Meta's AI age-estimation technology now scans Instagram accounts worldwide, placing millions of teens into stricter safety settings automatically.
item.content:encoded:
My own niece has told me for years that she and her friends could get around age restrictions on Facebook and Instagram when they were younger. They knew how easy it was to make themselves appear older online. And I suspect plenty of parents have heard similar stories. So when I heard that Meta was expanding its AI technology to identify teens who lie about their age, my first thought was, it's about time.

On November 9, Meta announced a worldwide expansion of its AI age-estimation technology. The system looks for accounts that may belong to teenagers, even when someone has entered an adult birthday. Meta says the expansion will place millions more young users into Instagram's built-in Teen Account protections.

The move comes as lawsuits and growing public pressure push Meta to take greater responsibility for protecting young users. After years of concerns about children getting around social media age restrictions, this could be one of the company's most significant attempts yet to address the problem. But how does Instagram's AI figure out someone's age? And can parents trust it to get things right?

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

FRANCE BECOMES FIRST EU NATION TO BAN SOCIAL MEDIA FOR CHILDREN UNDER 15

For years, entering a birthday was one of the easiest ways to tell Instagram how old you were. The problem was that the app had to rely heavily on what someone told it. Now Meta is using artificial intelligence to look for clues that suggest an account belongs to someone under 18. Instead of relying solely on the birthday listed on a profile, the company's age-estimation technology analyzes account activity and other signals to estimate whether someone may be a teenager.

Meta has previously explained that its age-detection technology can look for clues such as birthday celebrations, references to school grades and information shared in posts or comments. The company has also described separate technology that analyzes photos and videos to help identify accounts belonging to children under 13. According to the company, that technology examines general visual clues without using facial recognition or identifying specific people.

The important thing to understand is that these systems estimate age. They don't establish someone's exact birthday. If Instagram's AI determines that an account likely belongs to someone between 13 and 17, the company can automatically apply Teen Account protections. That means a teenager who entered an adult birthday could suddenly find their account operating under stricter safety settings.

Instagram's Teen Accounts have been around since 2024. However, those protections depend on the platform correctly identifying younger users. The new worldwide expansion is designed to close that gap. When Meta identifies an account that likely belongs to a teenager, it can apply safeguards that include:

Teens under 16 generally need parental permission to make built-in safety settings less restrictive. Instagram has also introduced 13+ content settings inspired by PG-13 movie ratings. Those filters are designed to reduce the amount of mature material younger users encounter.

We previously covered how Instagram's PG-13 restrictions give parents more control over what teens see. Of course, no content filter catches everything. And these protections can only help if Instagram correctly identifies the accounts that need them.

ROBLOX SHARES AI CHILD-SAFETY TOOLS PARENTS SHOULD KNOW

Meta began testing AI technology to identify teens using adult birthdays in the United States in April 2025. The company later expanded the system to additional countries, including Australia, Canada and the United Kingdom. In May 2026, Meta announced further expansion into the European Union and Brazil. Now the technology is going global.

According to Meta, millions more teens will receive additional safety protections, even if they originally claimed to be adults. The company is also expanding age-detection technology on Facebook, with a similar rollout planned for Threads later in 2026.

Meanwhile, Meta says it has started using Apple's age-range signal in Australia. With the right permissions, Apple's system can share someone's age range with participating apps. That gives Meta another way to check whether someone meets an app's age requirements. The big question is whether all this technology will finally make it harder for kids to get around the rules.

The timing of this announcement is worth paying attention to. For years, parents and child safety advocates have raised concerns about social media platforms and their effects on young users. Meanwhile, Meta has faced lawsuits alleging that its platforms contribute to harmful experiences for children and teenagers. Meta reportedly reached settlements worth up to approximately $18 billion with nearly every U.S. state and territory in August 2026. The agreements address lawsuits brought by attorneys general over alleged harm to teens. Under those agreements, Meta committed to strengthening how it identifies teenagers and children younger than 13.

The settlement also includes stronger controls for teens in participating U.S. jurisdictions, including a default two-hour daily limit across Facebook and Instagram that requires parental permission to disable. Additional provisions address nighttime access and parental oversight. Those commitments are separate from the new worldwide AI expansion, although they reflect the broader pressure Meta faces.

And there's an important point here. Meta has known for years that younger users sometimes enter false birthdays. The challenge has been figuring out how to identify them reliably. The company has introduced safety features over time. But public criticism and legal action have increased the pressure to show that those features actually work. Meta's latest announcement suggests the company is putting more resources behind age detection. The results will determine whether this becomes a meaningful turning point. We reached out to Meta for comment on its expanded AI age checks, but did not hear back before our deadline.

That's another concern worth examining. AI can make mistakes, particularly when it tries to draw conclusions from someone's online activity. An adult might regularly post photos of younger relatives. Someone could also share old school pictures or birthday celebrations from years ago. That doesn't mean one post will automatically convince Instagram that an adult is a teenager. Meta uses multiple signals when making age estimates. However, mistakes remain possible.

Meta says people who are incorrectly placed into Teen Account settings can take steps to verify their age and restore the appropriate settings. Depending on the situation, Instagram may require proof of age through identification or an age-estimation service. And there's another side to the problem. The technology could miss teenagers who successfully make their accounts appear to belong to adults.

That's why parents should still review their children's account settings rather than assuming Instagram has correctly identified their age. Meta's November 9 announcement did not provide a new accuracy figure for the worldwide expansion. I'd like to see more information about how often the system gets these decisions right and how quickly people can correct mistakes.

CHRIS HANSEN URGES PARENTS TO TEACH CHILDREN ABOUT ONLINE PREDATORS BEFORE ALLOWING INTERNET ACCESS

Starting in November 2026, Meta says parents in the United States will begin seeing an informational video in their Instagram feeds. The video will explain how Meta identifies teenagers and places them into age-appropriate protections. It will also link to guidance from internet safety advocate Larry Magid, president and CEO of ConnectSafely.

The guidance explains Meta's approach to identifying younger users and how parents can help ensure their children's ages are accurate. Parents worldwide can also access age-assurance resources through Meta's Family Center. For families, this creates an opportunity to have a conversation about why social media platforms ask for someone's age in the first place.

Even with stronger AI protections, I wouldn't leave everything up to Instagram. There are several practical steps parents can take right now.

Ask your teen to open Instagram and go to their profile. Tap the menu, open Accounts Center, then look for Personal details and Birthday. Make sure the birthday is accurate. Instagram may require verification if someone attempts to change an account's age from under 18 to an adult age.

Open Instagram's settings and look for the account privacy controls. Check whether the account is private and review who can follow your teen. Also review who can send messages. You may find that some protections are already enabled through Teen Accounts.

Instagram's Family Center gives parents additional tools for managing a teen's experience. Parental supervision requires both the parent and teen to agree to the connection. Once connected, parents can review available safety controls and manage certain account restrictions.

Instagram offers daily usage reminders and additional restrictions for teens. Parents can also use supervision settings to manage screen time. On an iPhone, open Settings, then Screen Time to review available app limits. For Android devices, Google Family Link offers parental controls and device management options.

Instagram's 13+ content setting is designed to limit material that may be inappropriate for teenagers. Parents can review these protections and choose stricter settings where available. Remember that filters may still miss content, so it's worth asking your teen what regularly appears in their feed.

This may be the most useful step. Ask your teen whether they have ever felt tempted to enter an older birthday to unlock features or avoid restrictions. Explain that providing the correct age helps Instagram apply protections intended for younger users. And make sure they know they can talk to you if they encounter something uncomfortable online.

It's about time. My own niece told me years ago how easily she and her friends could get around the age restrictions on Facebook and Instagram. And I remember wondering why these platforms weren't doing more about it. Now, with lawsuits mounting and public pressure growing, Meta is finally taking a bigger step to address the problem. I'm glad to see it, but I want to know how well this AI actually works. Will it catch teens who lie about their age? And what happens when it gets someone's age wrong? Parents have been asking for better protections for years. It's time for Meta to show that these changes are making kids safer online.

Do you think Meta would be taking these steps without years of public pressure and lawsuits, or has the company finally realized it needs to do more to protect children online? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com
